# Project guidelines

This document is the source of truth for how Claude Code operates in
this codebase. We have invested in automation; the rules below keep
that automation predictable.

## Mission

Ship reliable infrastructure libraries to internal teams. Operate the
agent like a colleague: clear handoffs, written plans, observable
behavior.

## Languages and runtimes

- Node.js 20.10+.
- TypeScript 5.5 in strict mode.
- pnpm 9 with a committed lockfile.

## Repository layout

- `apps/` — applications.
- `packages/` — libraries.
- `tools/` — internal scripts.
- `infra/` — Terraform and deploy manifests.
- `docs/` — long-form docs and ADRs.

## Plan first

Plan mode is required for any change touching more than one file. Plans
list the goal, the files, and the test approach. Sub-agents read the
plan before executing.

## Hooks

We rely on three hooks, all defined in `settings.json` and stored in
`.claude/hooks/`:

- `pre-tool-use.sh` — logs the tool invocation to a local SQLite store.
- `post-tool-use.sh` — appends the tool's exit status to the same store.
- `stop.sh` — flushes the buffer and emits a session summary.

Hooks must exit 0 unless they want to halt the agent. Any non-zero exit
should be logged with a clear `[hook] reason: …` line.

## Sub-agents

Two sub-agents handle recurring work:

- `code-reviewer` — runs at the end of any feature branch.
- `release-driver` — drives a release end-to-end after the lead approves.

Sub-agent prompts live in `.claude/agents/<name>.md`. Frontmatter must
include `name` and `description`.

## Slash commands

Custom slash commands live in `.claude/commands/`. Today we ship
`/ship-it` for the release flow.

## Skills

Skills are small, single-purpose. We aggressively retire skills that
have not fired in 30 days.

## Testing

- Vitest for unit and integration; Playwright for end-to-end.
- One test file per module, co-located.
- No real network or disk outside `tmpdir()`.

## Linting and formatting

ESLint + Prettier are enforced in CI. Imports sorted alphabetically
within their group.

## Git workflow

- Branch from `main`.
- Conventional Commits.
- Squash merges, message under 72 chars.
- No force pushes to shared branches.

## Code review

Two approvals on any change touching `infra/` or shared `packages/*`.
One approval otherwise.

## Style

- Named exports.
- Pure functions; isolate I/O at the edges.
- Composition over inheritance.
- Throw on programmer errors; return Result-shaped values for expected
  failures.
- Functions ≤ 50 lines; files ≤ 250 lines.

## Comments

Comments explain *why*, not *what*.

## Dependencies

Pin direct dependencies. Audit transitive ones. Renovate keeps things
fresh.

## Performance

Optimize for clarity first. Profile before optimizing. Document hot
paths with a benchmark in `bench/`.

## Security

- Never commit secrets.
- Sanitize user input at the boundary.
- Subscribe to advisories for critical packages.

## Logging

- Shared `logger` package only.
- Structured JSON in production.
- Stable correlation ID per request.

## Error handling

- Cross-package errors subclass `BaseError` with a `.code`.
- Never swallow silently.

## File and directory naming

- `kebab-case` filenames.
- `<module>.test.ts` next to the module.
- `<name>.types.ts` for type-only files.

## Documentation

- JSDoc on every public function.
- ADRs in `docs/adr/NNNN-title.md`.

## CI

GitHub Actions: install, typecheck, lint, test, build, bundle-size
check, deploy-preview. A red step blocks merge.

## Releases

- `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` tags.
- Notes generated by `changesets`.
- `release-driver` sub-agent runs the flow.

## Working with Claude Code

- Read this file at session start.
- Plan mode for multi-file changes.
- Prefer reading files over guessing.
- Keep this file under 250 lines so it stays in working memory.

## Notes on this fixture

This file lives in the Operator fixture for the bench CLI test suite.
It is intentionally focused (~200 lines, well under the >300 penalty
bound) and structured with clear `##` headings to model what an
Operator-tier user has converged on.
